tells: B reads as Linear's homepage hero (dark UI, 'product development system for teams and agents')
B holds its headline as a blur for about 1.0s (0.5s to 1.4s) before it snaps sharp at 1.5s, so the first second of text is unreadable
B's product UI fades up as one block 1.6s to 2.3s; the only product action is a small agent panel appearing at the lower right at about 4.0s
A's card builds from an empty skeleton at 0.0s to full chart by 0.5s, then a cursor presses 'Find windows' at about 1.5s
A's scan line sweeps across the chart 1.7s to 2.5s and the wind bars turn amber as it passes, then '2 windows found' and the out/back windows land by 3.0s
A's proposed plan (08:30, 10:10, 12:30, 14:10) arrives at 3.5s and holds still to the end, about 2.5s

memorable.A: the scan line sweeping the forecast and the sailable windows lighting up behind it
memorable.B: the headline sharpening out of blur

corrections.problem: headline sits blurred and unreadable for about a second; the blur is decoration, not information
corrections.change: bring the headline in sharp with a short opacity and 8px rise over 0.4s so it is readable from 0.6s
corrections.keep: the dark field and the order headline, subhead, then product

corrections.problem: the whole app UI fades up as one flat block, so nothing in it owns the screen
corrections.change: let the frame land first, then reveal the issue pane and activity rows top to bottom with about 0.1s offsets
corrections.keep: the restrained fade and the position under the headline

corrections.where: B 4.00s, the agent panel at lower right
corrections.problem: the one product action is small, at the edge and arrives after attention has left
corrections.change: make the agent reply the climax: draw the eye to it with the rest of the UI held still, and hold its text at least 2.5s
corrections.keep: that the action happens inside the real UI, in place

corrections.problem: subhead and the small links at the right appear late and faint, competing with the UI fade
corrections.change: land the subhead with the headline, before the product starts moving
corrections.keep: the low contrast hierarchy of the subhead

tells: B reads as Stripe's homepage payments section ($5.46 terminal and 'Accept and optimize payments globally')
B's capture jumps from the hero to the section at 0.35s; that is a scroll in the filming, not the design, and I ignored it

B holds the $5.46 terminal and checkout still for about 4.7s, then every line rolls vertically in place to the German/euro version (Pay Roastery to Carby bezahlen, $5.46 to EUR 26.89) with rows staggered about 0.1s, done by 5.6s
B then holds the new state still for over 6s
A holds the finished plan for 6.0s, then washes the whole card to white 6.5s to 6.9s and restarts: the reset is a fade through blank, not an in-place change
A's cursor clicks 'Find windows' at about 7.8s, the scan sweeps 8.3s to 9.6s, windows land at 9.5s and the proposed plan grows the card's height at about 10.5s

memorable.A: the scan line lighting up the windows
memorable.B: the whole checkout rolling from dollars and English to euros and German in place

corrections.problem: the loop resets by fading the entire card to a near blank frame, which reads as a cut and throws away the reader's place
corrections.change: reset in place: roll the status back to 'Ready to check', fade the amber bars and windows out with the chart frame held still
corrections.keep: the 6s hold on the finished plan before the reset

corrections.where: A 9.50s to 10.50s, the proposed plan row
corrections.problem: the plan appears by growing the card taller, so the layout shifts under the windows just as they land
corrections.change: reserve the plan row's height from the start (placeholder or dimmed values) and fill it in place
corrections.keep: plan arriving after the windows, about 0.5s later

corrections.problem: cursor wanders across the chart for almost a second before the press, drawing the eye away from the chart
corrections.change: start the cursor near the button and press within 0.4s of the reset settling
corrections.keep: the visible press on 'Find windows' as the cause of everything after

corrections.where: A 8.30s to 9.60s, scan line and wind bars
corrections.problem: bars, stream, windows and status all change during the sweep, so no single thing owns the screen
corrections.change: let the scan own the sweep, then land the out window, then the back window, about 0.1s apart
corrections.keep: the scan line moving left to right in time

tells: A is the same Stripe payments sequence as trial 2 B; the jump at 0.35s is the capture scrolling
A holds the first state 4.8s, rolls every line in place 4.9s to 5.6s with row offsets near 0.1s, then holds 6s
B shows the old state (Forecast Fri 18:00, leave 11:10 to 13:45, 15:25) for only about 0.8s before it changes

B's change cascades in place about 0.1s apart: forecast badge rolls at 0.86s, end time 13:45 to 13:20 at 0.96s, the window gains a hatched cut at 1.06s, 15:25 rolls to 15:00, then the notification swaps at 1.16s to 1.36s
B's old notification fades to an empty card at 1.16s before the new text arrives, a brief blank
B then holds still for over 10s with nothing further happening

memorable.A: the checkout rolling into German and euros in place
memorable.B: the window end time rolling back and a hatched slice appearing on the bar

corrections.problem: the old forecast, window end 13:45 and 'Plan saved' are visible for under a second, so the viewer never reads what is about to change
corrections.change: hold the before state at least 2.5s, ideally with the 13:45 end time in a resting focus
corrections.keep: the in-place digit rolls and the 0.1s cascade

corrections.problem: the hatched slice is about 6px wide and is the actual news, but it is the smallest thing that moves
corrections.change: animate the window's right edge retracting from 13:45 to 13:20 over 0.4s with a landing ease, leaving the hatch behind
corrections.keep: the hatch pattern as the record of the lost time

corrections.problem: the old notification empties to a blank card before the new text appears, a visible gap
corrections.change: cross the texts in place (old out up, new in from below) with no empty frame
corrections.keep: the notification arriving last as the explanation

corrections.problem: everything is over by 1.4s and the remaining 10s are static, so the climax is crammed at the start
corrections.change: place the change after a 2.5s read and hold the result about 4s, then loop
corrections.keep: the long readable hold on the explanatory notification

tells: B is the same Stripe payments sequence again; first state held about 4.8s, in-place roll to the euro/German version 4.9s to 5.6s, then held over 6s
A draws the route leg by leg: the dot reaches Gurnard at about 1.4s and the readout changes Hamstead Ledge 09:17 4.6 nm to Gurnard 09:59 9.2 nm at 1.5s to 1.9s
A's readouts change by fading the label then the value about 0.1s apart, with a short frame where the label is blank
A arrives at Cowes at about 3.9s (10:10, 10.5 nm, 7.1 kn) and holds still for about 6s
A resets at 9.88s by fading the whole card to a fully blank frame at 10.08s, then the empty route reappears at 10.18s

memorable.A: the boat drawing the route to Cowes as the distance ticks up
memorable.B: the checkout switching currency and language in place

corrections.problem: the reset fades the card to a fully blank frame, a cut that loses the map and the reader's place
corrections.change: keep the map still and retract the route line back to Lymington in place, resetting the readout with a roll
corrections.keep: the long hold on the arrival before the reset

corrections.problem: values fade out and in, leaving a beat where the label is blank and the number is ghosted
corrections.change: roll the digits in place (09:17 to 09:59, 4.6 to 9.2 nm) so the number is never absent
corrections.keep: the label leading the value by about 0.1s

corrections.problem: the line and the dot move at near constant speed and stop at each waypoint without settling
corrections.change: ease each leg out so the dot decelerates into the waypoint, with a small settle on arrival at Cowes as the climax
corrections.keep: the leg-by-leg pacing of about 2s per leg

corrections.problem: arrival changes only the readout colour; the climax is no bigger than the waypoints before it
corrections.change: mark arrival once: the Cowes pin fills and the 10:10 lands a beat after, with the rest held still
corrections.keep: the magenta arrival time and the restraint of a single accent
